## 1. Persona and outcome

As a **<role>**, I need to **<job-to-be-done>**, so that **<measurable outcome>**.

Keep the optional `catalog` frontmatter aligned with this approved narrative,
or remove it if no structured projection is wanted. Catalog/dashboard and MCP
search derive its fields directly from this specification; do not copy them
to catalog metadata. Text values or `en`/`it`/`source` maps are supported.
Unresolved frontmatter placeholders block preparation. Spec-sync preserves
frontmatter; it never invents business metadata from free-form prose.

## 4. Technical reference

After manifest/import exists, save the narrative without technical tables.
Preview `mcp-kit spec-sync <id>`, then add `--write` with local-write approval.
The generator appends a marked block of actual operation IDs/routes/statuses.
Do not copy or edit those tables. Keep purpose/confirmation decisions in the
narrative. Spec-sync preserves everything outside its block, and refuses
unmarked legacy tables until they are deliberately reviewed/migrated.

## 5. Data structures

Describe required data in business terms; reference the actual contract schemas
instead of duplicating them. Use `mcp-kit catalog --source builtin --schemas`
during discovery and `scenario-contract` for the imported client afterward.

## 7. Mock behavior

Describe which real examples/rules support the storyline. Response status tables
are generated by spec-sync; do not rewrite them. Inspect actual examples and
x-mock through scenario-contract. Request conditions/dialogue require review.

Mocks use response examples and `x-mock` only. They do not maintain state or
calculate business outcomes.
